Counsel for Petitioner :- Shailendra Kumar Misra

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard the counsel for the petitioner and the learned Standing Counsel.

2. The present petition has been filed challenging the order dated 24.07.2024 whereby the application filed by the petitioner for payment of compensation to the extent of one half of the portion for which there is no dispute has been rejected.

3. The neat contention of the counsel for the petitioner is that the amounts were deposited before the Tribunal and the payments are governed by virtue of Section 77 of the Land Acquisition Act,
2013.

He draws my attention to the fact that the original land holding belonged to Sheetal and Teja,

sentences.text: the family tree of said two persons has been enclosed.

4. The submission of the counsel for the petitioner is that the legal heirs flowing from the family tree of Teja are owner to the extent of one half of the property, which was acquired and there is no dispute amongst them, however a dispute was raised by one Sarju Dei along with two others persons in respect of the legal heir who were entitled to compensation and belonged to the family tree flowing from Sheetal.
He draws my attention to the specific pleadings to that effect.
5. In short, the submission is that there is no dispute with regard to compensation within the family of Teja and thus, half the amount to which they are entitled should be paid.

He further argues that there is no dispute with regard to the entitlement of half of the amount in between the parties as is evident from the pleadings and this aspect has not been considered by the Tribunal while passing the impugned order.
6. A perusal of the impugned order reveals that the application has been rejected solely on the ground that Sarju Dei has filed objections with regard to payment.

It was incumbent upon the Tribunal to have seen the pleadings of Sarju Dei which prima-facie relate to the apportionment of compensation in respect of the owners flowing from Sheetal and a specific pleading has been raised by her that she has no objection if the amount is paid to the family of Teja.
7. Considering the fact that the petitioners are suffering from 2004, the order dated 24.07.2024 is quashed.

The matter is remanded to the Tribunal to pass a fresh order taking into consideration the specific pleadings and objections as contained in para 3 of the objections and pass a fresh order within a period of six weeks from the date of filing of a copy of this order and the court concerned assuming the jurisdiction.
8. The writ petition stands disposed off in terms of the said order.

Order Date :- 12.11.2024 VNP/-
